name: Disk imaging and acquisition
intro: Every examination starts with a verified copy. These tools image drives, verify hashes and mount images so the original evidence is never touched.

name: Computer and disk forensics suites
intro: All-in-one platforms that open a disk image, parse the file system and artifacts, and let you search, bookmark and report in one place.

name: File recovery and carving
intro: When files are deleted or the file system is damaged, carvers rebuild them from raw data using file signatures.

name: Windows artifacts and registry
intro: Windows records what users and programs did in the registry, the MFT, prefetch, shellbags and many other places. These tools read them.

name: Memory (RAM) forensics
intro: RAM holds what the disk never sees: running processes, network connections, decrypted data and fileless malware. First acquire a memory image, then analyse it.

name: Mobile forensics: Android
intro: Tools to extract data from Android devices and to parse app databases, logs and backups into something readable.

name: Mobile forensics: iOS
intro: Tools to create and read iPhone and iPad backups and to parse the system and app artifacts inside them.

name: macOS forensics
intro: Collection and parsing tools for Mac artifacts such as unified logs, pattern-of-life databases and persistence items.

name: Linux forensics
intro: Live response collectors and query tools for Linux and other Unix-like systems.

name: Network forensics and PCAP
intro: Capture traffic, rebuild what was transferred and turn packets into searchable logs.

name: Log and event analysis
intro: Tools that parse event logs and hunt through them with detection rules, so thousands of events become a short list of leads.

name: Timeline analysis
intro: Build one ordered timeline from many artifacts, then explore it to see what happened and when.

name: Incident response and triage
intro: Collect the most important evidence from live systems quickly, across one machine or thousands, and manage the case.

name: Malware analysis and reversing
intro: Static and dynamic analysis tools for understanding what a suspicious file does. Always work in an isolated virtual machine.

name: Cloud forensics
intro: Collect and analyse logs and resources from Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud and containers.

name: Email forensics
intro: Read mailbox files and analyse message headers to trace where an email really came from.

name: Browser forensics
intro: Recover history, downloads, cache, cookies and stored data from web browsers.

name: Database and SQLite forensics
intro: Most app data lives in SQLite. These tools browse databases and recover deleted records.

name: Image, video and audio forensics
intro: Inspect metadata, check images for editing and examine audio and video recordings.

name: Password recovery and decryption
intro: Recover passwords and open encrypted volumes when you have the legal authority to do so.

name: OSINT and social media
intro: Gather and preserve publicly available information about people, accounts and domains.

name: Drone and IoT forensics
intro: Decode drone flight logs and take apart the firmware of embedded and smart devices.

name: Cryptocurrency forensics
intro: Look up transactions and addresses on public blockchains and work with wallet data found in evidence.

name: Hashing, hex and utilities
intro: The small everyday tools: hashing, hex editing, decoding data and converting timestamps.

name: Forensic distros and lab environments
intro: Ready-made Linux distributions and lab builds that come with many forensic tools already installed.

name: Forensic file copy and disk cataloguing
intro: Copy selected files with their timestamps intact and a log of what was copied, or list what is on a disk without imaging all of it.

name: Software write blocking
intro: A write blocker stops the examination computer from changing the evidence drive. These are software options for when a hardware blocker is not available. Test any write blocker before you trust it.

name: Media sanitisation and drive re-use
intro: Wipe drives before re-using them for evidence, so that old data cannot contaminate a new case, and verify that the wipe worked.

name: String and keyword search
intro: Find words, patterns and readable text inside files, folders and raw data.

name: Instant messenger forensics
intro: Decrypt, parse and export chats from messaging apps such as WhatsApp, Signal, Discord and Microsoft Teams.

name: Steganalysis
intro: Detect and extract data hidden inside images and audio, and create test files to learn how hiding works.

name: Video analysis and conversion
intro: Play, inspect and convert video, including awkward formats exported from CCTV systems.

name: GPS and location forensics
intro: Convert, plot and analyse location data from devices, apps and photos.

name: Vehicle and infotainment forensics
intro: Capture and decode vehicle CAN bus data. Free tools for infotainment units themselves are rare.

name: Wi-Fi forensics
intro: Detect wireless networks and devices, capture wireless traffic and look up where a network has been seen.

name: VoIP forensics
intro: Rebuild and inspect internet phone calls and their signalling from captured traffic.

name: Peer-to-peer (P2P) analysis
intro: Examine the files and settings left behind by file-sharing clients such as BitTorrent.

name: Remote forensics
intro: Collect evidence from computers over the network instead of visiting each one.

name: Case tracking and reporting
intro: Keep track of incidents, findings, timelines and notes, and turn them into a report.

name: Data analytics and visualisation
intro: Explore large sets of evidence data, clean them up and turn them into charts, graphs and maps.

name: Tool testing and validation
intro: Reference data sets and published test methods for checking that a forensic tool gives correct results.
